title: NewByteArray、GetPrimitiveArrayCritical 与 DirectByteBuffer 内存归属
key_conclusions: NewByteArray creates Java heap byte arrays whose long-term ownership must be verified with HPROF and JNI/Java retained paths.
GetByteArrayElements can expose either a copy or pinned array data, so every path must call ReleaseByteArrayElements with the correct mode.
GetPrimitiveArrayCritical should be held only for very short non-blocking memory access windows because prolonged critical sections can interfere with GC behavior.
DirectByteBuffer separates a Java wrapper from native memory ownership, requiring both HPROF wrapper checks and native heap/showmap/heapprofd release evidence.
shallow_points: The article does not include a real Perfetto trace showing GC or pause impact from a long GetPrimitiveArrayCritical section.
It does not validate copy-versus-pin behavior against a target ART branch or device runtime state.
It does not include a runnable NDK sample for NewByteArray retention, GetByteArrayElements release modes, critical arrays, and DirectByteBuffer ownership.
It does not include real heapprofd/showmap/HPROF artifacts proving DirectByteBuffer wrapper and native memory lifetimes diverge.

Day 27's meminfo bucket model provides the acceptance gate for Java Heap versus Native Heap divergence.
